youtube_title: Schererville and Dyer, Indiana: the lake that was drained away, and the ditch that killed its owner
youtube:
You asked for Schererville! There was once a shallow lake between Dyer and Schererville, Indiana. A ditch made it disappear. It was called Lake George (not the one in Hammond or Hobart). It lay between Dyer, Hartsdale and Schererville, with swamp around it. Aaron Hart, a former Philadelphia book publisher, bought swamp land there. A big ditch was dug, five miles to the Little Calumet River. The lake drained away. Thousands of acres became farmland. On January 12, 1883, Hart stood in the bottom of a new ditch on his farm at Dyer. The left bank caved in without warning. He was killed instantly. The big ditch still carries his name: Hart Ditch. That Lake George is gone. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Schererville #Dyer #LakeCountyIndiana #TheRegion #HartDitch #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; no one is shown in the ditch. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900); T. H. Ball, 'The Cady Marsh', Proceedings of the Indiana Academy of Science; Encyclopedia of Genealogy and Biography of Lake County, Indiana (1904), quoting the local press of 1883; Town of Dyer, History of Dyer; U.S. Geological Survey (Hart Ditch at Munster). More local history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
